title: About Eric Davis | Web Designer & SEO Strategist
meta: Eric Davis: 9 years at Kaiser Permanente, now bringing enterprise-level web strategy to independent businesses in Los Angeles.
blocks: I didn't learn business from a textbook.

I learned it by starting at the bottom. Call centers, reception desks, processing claims, talking to real people solving real problems. That experience taught me something important: most business problems aren't technology problems. They're clarity problems. That's where I come in.
I care more about outcomes than websites.

A lot of web designers start with colors, fonts, and layouts. I start with questions. Why aren't customers finding you? Why aren't visitors converting? Why are competitors showing up ahead of you? What's actually stopping your business from growing?

Sometimes the answer is a website redesign. Sometimes it's SEO. Sometimes it's your messaging. Sometimes it's something nobody has pointed out yet. My job isn't to sell you a website. My job is to help you make better business decisions online. I've spent nearly a decade inside one of the country's largest healthcare organizations, managing 13 enterprise websites on Adobe Experience Manager and running domain governance programs that protect multi-billion dollar brands. I've sat in the rooms where real decisions get made.

I've watched organizations spend enormous amounts of money solving problems that could have been prevented with better planning. I've also seen small businesses get sold services they never needed. That's one of the reasons I started Davis Digital Studio. Independent businesses deserve strategic thinking without agency overhead, inflated retainers, or confusing jargon. You shouldn't have to spend $50,000 to get good advice.
I'm also a first-generation college student currently finishing my M.S. in Business Analytics at CSUN as a Dean's Scholar. I bring the same discipline to every client project.
Work hard. Live well. Do both.

I grew up working. First-gen, started from the bottom of an org chart and worked up through nine roles to get where I am. That's not a sob story, it's a competitive advantage. I know what it actually takes to build something from nothing, and I bring that same energy to every client I work with.
Started at Kaiser Permanente in member services. Learned how the business actually runs from the ground up.
Moved into digital content, managing B2B pages across enterprise websites on Adobe Experience Manager.
Stepped into IT as a digital content producer, then took on the Domain Management program, building governance from scratch, managing vendor relationships, and running brand protection proceedings.
Launched on Juneteenth, a freelance practice focused on small and mid-size businesses. First client: Bacchus Kitchen, Pasadena.
Dean's Scholar, graduating May 2026. Applying data science to web strategy: keyword modeling, performance analysis, and ROI forecasting.
If I don't think something will help your business, I'll tell you. Even if it means less work for me.
A beautiful website that nobody finds is still a failure. Every recommendation starts with business goals, customer behavior, and measurable outcomes.
I don't disappear after launch. I want clients who see me as a long-term resource, not someone they hired once and never hear from again.

No sales presentation. No pressure. No obligation. Just a conversation about your business, your goals, and what's getting in the way. If I can help, I'll tell you how. If I can't, I'll tell you that too.

meta: Web design and local SEO for gyms, yoga studios, therapists, chiropractors, and wellness practices. Get found on Google and grow your client base.
blocks: Trust starts long before the first appointment.

When someone is looking for a therapist, trainer, chiropractor, or wellness provider, they're not just looking for a service. They're looking for someone they can trust. Your website should help them feel that trust before they ever contact you.
Why businesses like yours struggle to grow online
Wellness clients need to trust you before they book. If your website doesn't build that trust quickly, they move on to someone whose does.
No clear first step for new clients
Someone visiting for the first time is anxious about getting started. Your website needs to answer "what do I do first?" with a simple, obvious next step on every page.
People choose wellness providers based on personal fit and trust. Bios, credentials, photos, and your approach need prominent placement, not buried in a tiny About page.
Not showing up for local searches
"Therapist near me," "yoga studio [city]," "personal trainer [neighborhood]", these are high-intent searches. If you're not in the top 3, those clients go to someone who is.
A contact form is not a booking system. Every extra step between "I'm interested" and "I have an appointment" loses clients to practices with frictionless online scheduling.
When someone searches for what you offer, your website should be the first thing they see.
A site that builds trust before the first appointment, makes scheduling effortless, and brings new clients through Google every week.
Acuity, Jane, Mindbody, or SimplePractice booking built into every page. New client intake forms, appointment types, and cancellation policies handled cleanly.
Detailed bios with photos, credentials, specialties, and your approach to treatment. Trust is built before they walk in, and a strong bio is also a local SEO asset.
Clear, readable descriptions of each service, session length, and pricing. Transparency reduces the friction of the first call and attracts better-fit clients from the start.
On-page optimization targeting your specific modalities, location, and client type. Google Business Profile setup with photos, Q&A, and a review response strategy.
Social proof from existing clients structured with schema markup so Google shows your star rating in search results before anyone even clicks your link.
What to expect on your first visit, what to bring, insurance questions, all answered on the site. Reduces pre-appointment anxiety and the volume of "just checking" phone calls.

Most small businesses have never done real SEO. That means every day, customers who need exactly what you offer are finding your competitors instead.

Your Google Business Profile is incomplete
